items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: I never heard of them doing anything like that.

ctx.x: Well, I didn't know. They had some down there, but I didn't know them. I just know about people saying what they do, you know, for a living. They trapping, picking moss and do trapping. The moss, they had a club. The moss pickles and the coon trappers. That was the name of the club, and they all used to congregate there. Did you play for them? No, I never did play for them. What kind of people were they? Well, they were all right. They were... Page okay? Oh, yeah, okay. They were... Just ordinary people. And you…

I was talking... Do you know Kid Shee, Koloff? He plays trumpet with the Olympiad man. He was saying that he was playing down in the Ninth Ward, and that second line said you're going to have to share that money.
Oh, no. You know? You know, the people do so many different things. Now, they didn't do then. But I never heard of them doing anything like that. But I wouldn't say that they wouldn't.
